requirements.text: Public" without the use of quotes, see Section 4.1 of [RFC5322]), but agents MUST NOT generate productions of such syntax.

requirements.heading: Base
requirements.text: Agents conforming to this specification MUST generate only conformant articles.

requirements.heading: Header Fields
requirements.text: o All agents MUST generate header fields so that at least one space immediately follows the ':' separating the header field name and the header field body (for compatibility with deployed software, including NNTP [RFC3977] servers).

requirements.heading: Header Fields
requirements.text: News agents MAY accept header fields that do not contain the required space.

requirements.heading: Header Fields
requirements.text: o Every line of a header field body (including the first and any that are subsequently folded) MUST contain at least one non- whitespace character.

requirements.heading: Header Fields
requirements.text: o Compliant software MUST NOT generate (but MAY accept) header field lines of more than 998 octets.

requirements.heading: Header Fields
requirements.text: Where the use of non-ASCII characters is required, they MUST be encoded using the MIME mechanisms defined in [RFC2047] and [RFC2231].

requirements.heading: MIME Conformance
requirements.text: User agents MUST meet the definition of MIME conformance in [RFC2049] and MUST also support [RFC2231].

requirements.heading: MIME Conformance
requirements.text: User agents MAY accept and generate other MIME extension header fields, and in particular SHOULD accept Content-Disposition [RFC2183] and Content-Language [RFC3282].

requirements.heading: News Header Fields
requirements.text: Each of these header fields MUST NOT occur more than once in a news article.

requirements.heading: Mandatory Header Fields
requirements.text: Each Netnews article conformant with this specification MUST have exactly one of each of the following header fields: Date, From, Message-ID, Newsgroups, Path, and Subject.

requirements.heading: Date
requirements.text: Therefore, agents MUST accept <date-time> constructs that use the "GMT" zone.

requirements.heading: Date
requirements.text: NOTE: This specification does not change [RFC5322], which says that agents MUST NOT generate <date-time> constructs that include any zone names defined by <obs-zone>.

requirements.heading: Date
requirements.text: Software that accepts dates with unknown timezones SHOULD treat such timezones as equivalent to "-0000" when comparing dates, as specified in Section 4.3 of [RFC5322].

requirements.heading: Message-ID
requirements.text: The <msg-id> MUST NOT be more than 250 octets in length.

requirements.heading: Message-ID
requirements.text: Implementations MUST NOT generate a Message-ID where the only difference from another Message-ID is the case of characters in the <id-right> part.

requirements.heading: Message-ID
requirements.text: When generating a <msg-id>, implementations SHOULD use a domain name as the <id-right>.

requirements.heading: Newsgroups
requirements.text: Optional FWS in the <newsgroup-list> SHOULD NOT be generated, but MUST be accepted.

requirements.heading: Newsgroups
requirements.text: A <component> SHOULD NOT consist solely of digits and SHOULD NOT contain uppercase letters.

requirements.heading: Newsgroups
requirements.text: Such <component>s MAY be used only to refer to existing groups that do not conform to this naming scheme, but MUST NOT be used otherwise.

requirements.heading: Newsgroups
requirements.text: <component>s beginning with underline ("_") are reserved for use by future versions of this standard and SHOULD NOT be generated by user agents (whether in header fields or in newgroup control messages as defined by [RFC5537]).

requirements.heading: Newsgroups
requirements.text: However, such names MUST be accepted by news servers.

requirements.heading: Newsgroups
requirements.text: <component>s beginning with "+" and "-" are reserved for private use and SHOULD NOT be generated by user agents (whether in header fields or in newgroup control messages [RFC5537]) without a private prior agreement to do so.

requirements.heading: Newsgroups
requirements.text: The following <newsgroup-name>s are reserved and MUST NOT be used as the name of a newsgroup:

requirements.heading: Newsgroups
requirements.text: The following <newsgroup-name>s have been used for specific purposes in various implementations and protocols and therefore MUST NOT be used for the names of normal newsgroups.

requirements.heading: Newsgroups
requirements.text: They MAY be used for their specific purpose or by local agreement.

requirements.heading: Control
requirements.text: An article with a Control header field MUST NOT also have a Supersedes header field.

requirements.heading: Distribution
requirements.text: "world" indicates unlimited distribution and SHOULD NOT be used explicitly, since it is the default when the Distribution header field is absent entirely.

requirements.heading: Distribution
requirements.text: "All" MUST NOT be used as a <dist-name>.

requirements.heading: Distribution
requirements.text: <dist-name>s SHOULD contain at least three characters, except when they are two-letter country codes drawn from [ISO3166-1].

requirements.heading: Distribution
requirements.text: Optional FWS in the <dist-list> SHOULD NOT be generated, but MUST be accepted.

requirements.heading: Followup-To
requirements.text: The Followup-To header field SHOULD NOT appear in a message, unless its content is different from the content of the Newsgroups header field.

requirements.heading: Followup-To
requirements.text: Agents MUST generate the keyword "poster" in lowercase, but MAY choose to recognize case- insensitive forms such as "Poster".

requirements.heading: Followup-To
requirements.text: As in the Newsgroups (Section 3.1.4) header field, optional FWS in the <newsgroup-list> SHOULD NOT be generated, but MUST be accepted.

requirements.heading: Injection-Date
requirements.text: This header field MUST be inserted whenever an article is injected.

requirements.heading: Injection-Date
requirements.text: However, software that predates this standard does not use this header, and therefore agents MUST accept articles without the Injection-Date header field.

requirements.heading: Injection-Date
requirements.text: Agents MUST NOT alter a pre-existing Date header field when adding an Injection- Date header field.

requirements.heading: Injection-Info
requirements.text: Other <attribute>s SHOULD NOT be used unless defined in extensions to this standard.

requirements.heading: Injection-Info
requirements.text: If non-standards-based <attribute>s are used, they MUST begin with an "x-".

requirements.heading: Injection-Info
requirements.text: Although comments and folding of whitespace are permitted throughout the Injection-Info header field, folding SHOULD NOT be used within any <parameter>.

requirements.heading: Injection-Info
requirements.text: Folding SHOULD only occur before or after the ";" separating <parameter>s, and comments SHOULD only be used following the last <parameter>.

requirements.heading: Injection-Info
requirements.text: In order to limit the exposure of personal data, it SHOULD be given in a form that cannot be interpreted by other sites.

requirements.heading: Injection-Info
requirements.text: However, to make it useful for rate limiting and abuse detection, two messages posted from the same source SHOULD have the same value of "posting-account", and two messages from different sources SHOULD have differing values of "posting-account".

requirements.heading: References
requirements.text: o The updated <msg-id> construct defined in Section 3.1.3 MUST be used.

requirements.heading: References
requirements.text: o Message identifiers MUST be separated with CFWS.

requirements.heading: References
requirements.text: o Comments in CFWS between message identifiers can cause interoperability problems, so comments SHOULD NOT be generated but MUST be accepted.

requirements.heading: User-Agent
requirements.text: This header field MAY contain multiple <product> tokens identifying the user agent and any subproducts that form a significant part of it, listed in order of their significance for identifying the application.

requirements.heading: Obsolete Header Fields
requirements.text: These header fields MUST NOT be generated and SHOULD be ignored.

requirements.heading: Lines
requirements.text: All agents SHOULD ignore it and SHOULD NOT generate it.

requirements.heading: Security Considerations
requirements.text: Therefore, agents that generate message identifiers for Netnews articles SHOULD ensure that they are unpredictable.

requirements.heading: Informative References
requirements.text: o A SP (space) is REQUIRED after the colon (':') following a header field name.

requirements.heading: Informative References
requirements.text: o The length of a <msg-id> MUST NOT exceed 250 octets.

requirements.heading: Informative References
requirements.text: * The <obs-phrase> construct MUST be accepted.

requirements.heading: Informative References
requirements.text: * The obsolete <zone> "GMT" MUST be accepted within a <date-time>.
